Idempotency means that repeating the same request has the same intended effect as making it once. The important part is the effect of the request, rather than whether every detail of its execution stays identical.

For example, imagine sending a payment request with an idempotency key of `order-42`. If the first request creates a charge, repeating that request with the same key does not create a second charge in this hypothetical API. Each request can still add a log entry, so repetition may leave additional records even though the intended payment effect stays the same.

There is also a time limit. This API's stored result expires after 24 hours. After expiry, the same key is treated as new, so you cannot rely on it to prevent another charge.

Idempotency does not decide who may make the request. A request still needs authorization, even when it carries an idempotency key.
